Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Work & responsibility

skill noun

also skills, skilled, skilful, skillful

classical

Ov. Met. 3.588: ars illī sua cēnsus erat
Ter. Ad. 741

ars, artis f.

noun, third declension

skill; a craft, a trade

Skill in making or doing something, and the craft itself; a skill is ars, skills artēs. Skilled in, perītus with the genitive (see experience).

Other words

  • artificium, artificiī n. — skill, craftsmanship; a trade

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 53.3: memor artificiī meī; Traupman 158, 380

    Traupman’s word for skill; skilful is artificiōsus (Traupman 158, 380).

  • sollertia, sollertiae f. — skill, ingenuity, deftness

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.123: māchinātiō quaedam atque sollertia (Lewis & Short)

    Quick, inventive skill; also spelled sōlertia (Lewis & Short).

  • perītia, perītiae f. — practical skill, expertise

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Sall. Jug. 46.8: locōrum et mīlitiae (Lewis & Short)

    Skill that comes of experience; Sallust and Tacitus, not Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Ars illī sua cēnsus erat. Cum trāderet artem, «accipe quās habeō, studiī successor et hērēs,» dīxit «opēs.»

    His skill was his whole fortune. When he handed it on, he said: “Take what wealth I have, my successor and heir in the trade.”Ov. Met. 3.588–590

  • memor artificiī meī vetus frīgidae cultor mittō mē in mare

    mindful of my skill, an old devotee of cold water, I throw myself into the seaSen. Ep. 53.3

See also experience, practice, ability, ability, craftsman.
